# odyssey-002 (1.96–212) — new fixed renderings

Every choice below is a formula or epithet that plainly recurs and that the house table in
`conventions.md` does not yet cover. Format: **Greek — `l` — `i` — reason / what was avoided.**

Nothing here reopens a table entry. γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη (156, 178), ταλασίφρων (129), δαΐφρων (180),
νόστιμον ἦμαρ (168), νήσῳ ἐν ἀμφιρύτῃ (198, = 1.50) and ἁλός-type phrases are taken from the table
or from odyssey-001 unchanged.

## Whole-line and half-line formulas

| Greek | `l` | `i` | reason / avoided |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα (122) | "winged words he spoke" | "spoke winged words" | πτερόεις is πτερόν 'feather, wing' + -εις 'furnished with'; "winged" is the compound, not an interpretation of it. The phrase is worn smooth in English, but every alternative that avoids the cliché ("feathered words", "words that fly", "words with wings on them") either mistranslates the suffix or invents an English compound to be different. Kept on the same ground as "the father of men and of gods": generic and unavoidable. Avoided: "words winged and swift", "swift words". |
| τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε … (178) | "Him then in turn addressed" | "Then … spoke to him in turn" | A genuinely third reply-formula beside the table's τὸν/τὴν δ’ ἠμείβετ’ ἔπειτα ("Him then answered") and τὴν δ’ ἀπαμειβόμενος προσέφη ("Her answering addressed"). αὖτε 'in turn' is what distinguishes it and is carried into both layers so the reader can hear which formula is running. Avoided: collapsing it into "answered", which would make three formulas into one. |
| ἀλλ’ ἄγε μοι τόδε εἰπὲ καὶ ἀτρεκέως κατάλεξον (169, **206**) | "But come, tell me this, and recount it exactly" | "But come now, tell me this, and set it out for me exactly" | Repeats verbatim inside this part — Telemachus at 169, Athena turning it back on him at 206 — so the English is identical in both, differing only in the closing point the edition prints (`·` at 169, `,` at 206). κατάλεξον is 'recount in order, in full', not 'choose'; ἀτρεκέως is 'without swerving'. Avoided: "tell me truly" (that is ἐτήτυμον at 174), "tell me the whole truth". |
| χαῖρε, ξεῖνε (123) | "Welcome, stranger" | "Welcome, stranger" | χαῖρε is the ordinary word of greeting, an imperative of χαίρω. "Welcome" is what an English host says and is not archaic. Avoided: "Hail, stranger", "Greetings, stranger", "Joy to you", "Rejoice". |
| ξεῖνε φίλε (158) | "Dear stranger" | "Dear stranger" | φίλος here is 'dear', warmth to a guest just taken in; ξεῖνος is rendered "stranger" everywhere in this part, with the guest-friend sense carried by the note and by πατρώιος ξεῖνος below. Avoided: "friend", which drops ξεῖνος; "my dear guest", which drops the strangeness. |
| μνηστῆρες ἀγήνορες (106, 144) | "the lordly suitors" | "the lordly suitors" | ἀγήνωρ is usually taken as ἄγαν + ἀνήρ 'very manly'; in the Odyssey it leans towards 'overbearing'. "Lordly" carries both edges in one word. The derivation is not certain and the note says so. Avoided: "proud" (an interpretation), "manly" (wrong tone), "high-hearted" (imports a heart-word that is not in the compound). |
| πατρώιος ξεῖνος (176, 187) | "a guest-friend from my / our fathers' time" | "a guest-friend from my / our fathers' time" | The inherited ξενία that binds two houses. Avoided: "hereditary guest", "family friend", "a friend of my father's" — the last loses that the bond, not the acquaintance, is what is inherited. |

## Noun–epithet pairs and epithets

| Greek | `l` | `i` | reason / avoided |
|---|---|---|---|
| θεοειδής (113) | "godlike-in-form" | "godlike in form" | θεός + εἶδος. The table already fixes ἀντίθεος as "godlike"; since the house rule keeps distinct epithets distinct (cf. the three -φρων words), θεοειδής has to show its second element. Avoided: "godlike" flat, "of godlike form", "handsome as a god". |
| δῖος (Ὀδυσσεύς, 196) | "heavenly" | "heavenly" | The table already renders δῖα in δῖα θεάων as "heavenly-one"; the same word gets the same English wherever it stands, even where it sits oddly (the table's own principle, cf. *blameless* Aegisthus). The root is that of Ζεύς and the bright sky. Avoided: "divine" (reserved for θεῖος, so rendered at 1.65), "goodly", "brilliant", "noble". |
| ὀβριμοπάτρη (101) | "she of the mighty father" | "the daughter of a mighty father" | ὄβριμος + πατήρ, a title of Athena alone and about Zeus, not about her. Avoided: "mighty-fathered", "child of a mighty sire", "daughter of the Almighty". |
| Ταφίων ἡγήτωρ Μέντης (105, cf. 180–181) | "Mentes, the Taphians' leader" | "Mentes, the leader of the Taphians" | ἡγήτωρ from ἡγέομαι 'lead' — a leader of men, not a king (ἀνάσσω does that work at 181). Avoided: "chief", "lord", "prince of the Taphians". |
| φιλήρετμος (181) | "oar-loving" | "oar-loving" | φίλος + ἐρετμόν 'oar', transparent. Avoided: "that love the oar", "seafaring" (an inference, not the compound). |
| οἶνοψ πόντος (183) | "the wine-faced open-sea" | "the sea that has the look of wine" | ὄψ is 'look, face', the second element of γλαυκῶπις, which the table renders "gleaming-**eyed**". "Wine-dark" supplies a colour-word the Greek does not have and settles a question that has never been settled; `i` says what the compound says and no more. πόντος is "open-sea" as in odyssey-001. Avoided: "wine-dark sea", "wine-blue", "the purple sea". |
| ἀλλόθροοι ἄνθρωποι (183) | "men of other speech" | "men of another tongue" | ἄλλος + θρόος 'noise, speech'. Avoided: "foreigners", "men of strange speech", "barbarians" (βάρβαρος is not the word and not the idea). |
| αἴθων σίδηρος (184) | "fire-bright iron" | "fire-bright iron" | αἴθων is from αἴθω 'kindle, burn'; what it names in iron — the gleam, or the metal's colour — is disputed, and the note says so. "Fire-bright" keeps the burning root without settling the question. Avoided: "gleaming" (already in use for γλαυκῶπις), "flashing", "tawny", "ruddy". |
| πολυμήχανος (205) | "many-devising" | "a man of many devices" | πολύς + μηχανή 'device, contrivance'. A fourth compound epithet of Odysseus and kept apart from the table's δαΐφρων / πολύφρων / ταλασίφρων, which are all -φρων words; this one is not. Built on the same pattern as the table's "many-turning" for πολύτροπος. Avoided: "resourceful", "of many wiles", "never at a loss", "ingenious". |
| φίλη πατρὶς αἶα (203) | "his dear fatherland" | "his dear fatherland" | Keeps the "fatherland" of odyssey-001 at 1.75 (ἀπὸ πατρίδος αἴης) and adds φίλης as "dear"; αἶα is the by-form of γαῖα. Avoided: "his own dear native soil", "his beloved homeland". |
| κοίλῃς ἐνὶ νηυσίν (211) | "in hollow ships" | "in their hollow ships" | Generic and unavoidable: κοῖλος is 'hollow', of a hull. Recorded only so that it is fixed. Avoided: "in their curved ships", "in the deep-hulled ships". |
| αἰδοίη ταμίη (139) | "a revered housekeeper" | "a revered housekeeper" | αἰδοίη from αἰδώς is 'to be held in respect' and goes with the office rather than the scene; ταμίη is the woman who has charge of the stores. Avoided: "honoured", "grave", "modest", "the good housekeeper". |
| ὑλήεις (186) | "wooded" | "wooded" | From ὕλη. Kept distinct from δενδρήεσσα, which odyssey-001 renders "full-of-trees" at 1.51. Avoided: "leafy", "forested", "tree-clad". |
